reasoning_content: Login returned 200 rather than 302. Let me check the response body - maybe it succeeded and rendered? Actually successful sign_in typically redirects (302). 200 might mean login failed (rendered form again with error). But /admin still 302 means not authenticated. Let me inspect the response body for error.

action.command: cd /tmp && rm -f cj.txt && TOKEN=$(curl -s -c cj.txt http://127.0.0.1:3000/users/sign_in | grep -o 'name="authenticity_token" value="[^"]*"' | head -1 | sed 's/.*value="//;s/"//'); R=$(curl -s -b cj.txt -c cj.txt -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3000/users/sign_in --data-urlencode "authenticity_token=$TOKEN" --data-urlencode "user[email]=admin@consul.dev" --data-urlencode "user[password]=Aa12345678"); echo "$R" | grep -io "invalid[^<]*\|alert[^<]*\|error[^<]*" | head; echo "---cookie---"; cat cj.txt | grep -i session | head

tool_call.name: terminal
tool_call.arguments: {"command": "cd /tmp && rm -f cj.txt && TOKEN=$(curl -s -c cj.txt http://127.0.0.1:3000/users/sign_in | grep -o 'name=\"authenticity_token\" value=\"[^\"]*\"' | head -1 | sed 's/.*value=\"//;s/\"//'); R=$(curl -s -b cj.txt -c cj.txt -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3000/users/sign_in --data-urlencode \"authenticity_token=$TOKEN\" --data-urlencode \"user[email]=admin@consul.dev\" --data-urlencode \"user[password]=Aa12345678\"); echo \"$R\" | grep -io \"invalid[^<]*\\|alert[^<]*\\|error[^<]*\" | head; echo \"---cookie---\"; cat cj.txt | grep -i session | head", "security_risk": "LOW", "summary": "Inspect login response"}
